import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_2.csv"
]

# Read all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
dfs = [pd.read_csv(path, index_col=0) for path in source_files]

# According to the operation history, perform UNION of the three source tables
# All source tables have the same schema, so union (concat) is valid
df_union = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Enforce target schema and types:
# Target Schema: 
# 'username': float, 'date': string, 'retweets': integer, 'favorites': integer, 
# 'text': string, 'geo': string, 'mentions': string, 'hashtags': string, 
# 'id': float, 'permalink': string

# Convert columns to target types carefully

# username: float (source has NaN or string, convert strings to NaN and then float)
# Since examples show username as NaN, we convert all to float NaN
# But if there are any non-NaN strings, convert to NaN (cannot convert string usernames to float)
df_union['username'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['username'], errors='coerce')

# date: string (ensure string type)
df_union['date'] = df_union['date'].astype(str)

# retweets: integer
df_union['retweets'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['retweets'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# favorites: integer
df_union['favorites'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['favorites'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# text: string
df_union['text'] = df_union['text'].astype(str)

# geo: string (some NaN, convert NaN to None or keep as NaN)
df_union['geo'] = df_union['geo'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# mentions: string
df_union['mentions'] = df_union['mentions'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# hashtags: string
df_union['hashtags'] = df_union['hashtags'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# id: float
# Source id columns have large numbers, some in scientific notation, some as integers
df_union['id'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['id'], errors='coerce')

# permalink: string
df_union['permalink'] = df_union['permalink'].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']
df_target = df_union[target_columns]

# Write the result to the target path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/target_multisource.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join source1 and source2 to source0 on 'id' column (inner join to keep only matching ids)
df_join_01 = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))
df_join_all = pd.merge(df_join_01, source2, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_2'))

# After join, columns from different sources have suffixes; we need to reconstruct the target schema:
# Target schema: ['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']
# We will aggregate as follows:
# - group by 'id' (unique identifier, integer/float)
# - for string columns: take max (to pick non-null or lex max)
# - for numeric columns retweets, favorites: sum
# Note: username is float in target, but source has NaN, so max will keep NaN or a value if any

# Prepare aggregation dictionary
agg_dict = {
    'username': 'max',
    'date': 'max',
    'retweets': 'sum',
    'favorites': 'sum',
    'text': 'max',
    'geo': 'max',
    'mentions': 'max',
    'hashtags': 'max',
    'permalink': 'max'
}

# Group by 'id' and aggregate
df_final = df_join_all.groupby('id', as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_final = df_final[['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']]

# Write output CSV
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_14/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
